## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The change-event schema can contain fields the subscriber cannot access. Schema membership therefore must not serve as the application’s field authorization allowlist. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-security-field.html · keywords: Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization
- [statement] The Open WebUI advisory supplies a concrete cross-product failure example: a JWT revoked by sign-out or back-channel logout could still authenticate new realtime connections. This supports testing realtime revocation separately from HTTP; it is not evidence of a Salesforce vulnerability. (low confidence) — https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/security/advisories/GHSA-855v-hq7w-jmjw · keywords: Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization
- [statement] Security boundary caveat: Salesforce evaluates filter expressions even against fields the subscriber cannot access. Do not treat a matching filtered stream as proof that its predicate fields are authorized for the recipient. This caveat concerns authorization, not filter configuration. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-filter-considerations.html · keywords: Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Design inference: check each recipient’s Case read access before fan-out and again for alert history and details. Collector visibility alone does not establish recipient authorization: CDC ignores sharing, whereas record sharing normally limits which records a user can view. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-security-considerations.html · keywords: Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization · also: https://github.com/cfpb/salesforce-docs/blob/master/_pages/Record-Level-Sharing.md
- [statement] CDC checks field permissions for the subscribed user before delivery. In a shared collector, this protects the collector’s subscription; it does not establish the field permissions of each downstream alert recipient. The latter is a design inference requiring a separate recipient policy. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-security-field.html · keywords: Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization
- [statement] Design recommendation by analogy to Apache Superset’s notification policy: put only context-free change nudges on a shared broadcast scope; keep Case text and sensitive state out of that scope. Superset expressly prohibits sensitive or authoritative broadcast state. This is supporting engineering precedent, not a Salesforce guarantee. (low confidence) — https://github.com/apache/superset/blob/master/SECURITY.md · keywords: Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization
- [statement] For long-lived alert connections, revalidate authorization beyond connection establishment and handle session expiry. OWASP requires closing expired-session sockets; the WebSocket authentication guide warns against trusting a handshake indefinitely. Apply this principle to recipient access changes as a design requirement. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/blob/master/cheatsheets/WebSocket_Security_Cheat_Sheet.md · keywords: Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization · also: https://github.com/mattheworiordan/websocket.org/blob/main/src/content/docs/guides/authentication.md
- [statement] For the alert service, redact message payloads and credentials from logs. OWASP’s WebSocket guidance explicitly excludes complete messages, authentication tokens, session IDs, and personal information from logging. (low confidence) — https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/blob/master/cheatsheets/WebSocket_Security_Cheat_Sheet.md · keywords: Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization

## Research summary — Shared case-alert authorization and sensitive-data minimization

Shared Case alerting needs recipient authorization beyond collector access. Salesforce CDC ignores record sharing while checking the subscribed user’s field permissions; event schemas can expose field names beyond those permissions. The proposed alert service should check each recipient’s Case access before fan-out and when reading alert history or details. Apache Superset provides a useful precedent for keeping shared broadcasts free of sensitive state. OWASP and a realtime revocation advisory support separate handling of long-lived connection expiry, authorization, and payload redaction. These application design recommendations are distinguished from documented Salesforce behavior.
